text:
Sam W: paging oncall — multiple containers on gpu-node-17 started OOM'ing and we see CUDA illegal memory access in the logs, impacting a subset of inference routes. Anyone else seeing the same?

oncall-bot: @channel Incident created: INC-2026-0423. Severity: P1. Paging team: @ops-oncall-bot, @Maya R.

Maya R: confirmed. logs from the first container show repeated 'CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS' and then container restart loop. Affected model: llama-13b-cpu-hot (serving on GPU).

Leo K: dropping the latest GPU kernel module update? We pushed a microkernel tweak yesterday for packed-attn. Could be a kernel bug/race with the nvml path.

Irene C: attaching the snippet from dmesg (trimmed):
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=45321 sevm: illegal memory access at 0x7f8a2c000
[ 12345.679012] nvidia: GPU 0: GPU watchdog: hang
[ 12345.679123] containerd: container "svc:infer-abc" killed due to OOM
```

Sam W: thanks. nvml shows mem usage spike then GPU reset. This started ~10m after a canary deploy of optimize/packed-attn v2.

Maya R: impact: ~8% of hosted requests for dedicated customers experiencing 5xxs and elevated latency; autoscaler kicked new pods but some nodes flapped. Not universal — mainly gpu-node-17 and -18.

ops-oncall-bot: @ops-oncall-bot acknowledged. Handoff to oncall. Runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/gpu-illegal-address

Leo K: immediate mitigations I'm rolling: 1) cordon gpu-node-17, 2) drain non-critical pods (canary traffic), 3) redirect traffic to fallback model variant (quantized-llama-13b-v1) using routing policy.

Maya R: +1 to cordon. Also bumping retry backoff for client-side to reduce pressure. Starting canary rollback of packed-attn v2 to v1 on a subset.

Irene C: log from the crashed container's stacktrace (shortened):
```
libattention.so(+0x12f4a) [0x7f4c1a2f4a]
kernel: misaligned address check failed at kernel_attention.c:342
nvml:0x3 bad addr
```

Sam W: good to capture: are we seeing kernel-level misaligned pointer or a user-space out-of-bounds? Looks like kernel module complaining.

Leo K: initial hypothesis = a race introduced in packed-attn v2 where certain optimized kernels assume 256-byte alignment. For a subset of batches (odd seq len distribution) we end up with misaligned accesses that the GPU driver flags.

Maya R: mitigation timeline: cordon/drain done for gpu-node-17 (in progress for -18). Fallback routing enabled, error rate dropping from 8% -> 1.2% on routed customers. Canary rollback started, 3/5 canaries healthy so far.

Irene C: customer comms note: outages are transient and routed to fallback — no full data loss. Recommended message: "We observed transient GPU runtime errors causing elevated 5xxs for a subset of requests. We mitigated by rolling back a recent kernel-optimized deploy and routing traffic to a compatible model. We're investigating root cause and will follow up"

ops-oncall-bot: Suggested next steps: collect full coredump, nvdec logs, and kernel module version list from nodes. Run 'nvidia-bug-report.sh' on node with preserved logs.

Sam W: running dump now on gpu-node-17. Command: `sudo /usr/local/bin/nvidia-bug-report.sh --output /tmp/bugreport-17.tar.gz`

Leo K: also capturing the container image and exact commit hash of packed-attn: `git rev-parse --short HEAD` -> 9fa3b2c. I'll open a small reproducible with a crafted sequence-length distribution to stress the path.

Maya R: operational note: We should keep the fallback routing until a patch is validated. SLA impact tracker updated (incidents tracker link: https://internal/incidents/INC-2026-0423).

Irene C: assign follow-ups: Leo -> reproduce & patch; Maya -> customer comms + SLA; Sam -> logs & incident timeline; I'll coordinate postmortem.

ops-oncall-bot: Handoff reminder: next oncall available in 45m is @Sam W. Marking status: investigating -> mitigated (partial).

Sam W: thanks. I'll stay on until we have patch or safe kernel rollback. If reproduction is reliable, plan is to add alignment checks in runtime and a guarded fallback to safe kernel variant.

Leo K: quick note for devs — adding a test in CI to randomize tensor alignments to catch this class. Also adding an alignment assert around allocator.

Maya R: final for now: error count trending down, customers routed, rollback ongoing. Will update incident channel when we have confirmatory repro or hotfix. :white_check_mark:
